clue.text: Sediment is back in warehouse

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the storehouse word

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse or warehouse

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little word is from right to left

explanation.surface: A grumble about silt that has turned up inside a storage building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI, and 'in' puts SI inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is matter laid down by water, the settled layer at the bottom of a river or glass.

clue.text: I depart to scatter flies

indicators.note: to scatter means the letters of I depart are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone announces their departure in order to drive away the insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the insect order.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the zoological order of two-winged insects, the true flies such as houseflies and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Proper art Titian turned out in this capacity

definitions.text: Proper art Titian turned out in this capacity

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of the three words are produced in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The Venetian master produced genuine art while working as a painter of faces.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: Titian painted many likenesses, and his name with PROPER ART rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was famous for his likenesses of popes and kings, so this is the role in which he made proper art.

clue.text: Depression in the mining industry

parts.note: reads like an economic slump among miners, but means a physical hollow at the bottom of a mine shaft where water drains

explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit at the lowest point of a mine where water collects to be pumped out.

clue.text: Long time no see this bishop?

definitions.text: Long time no see this bishop?

parts.words: Long time no see this bishop?
parts.note: the greeting 'long time no see' is reread as a churchman who has never had a diocese of his own

explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's see is his diocese; one holding the rank in name only, with no real see, has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular bishop holds the title of an extinct diocese but governs no flock, a bishop in name only.

clue.text: Weariness is revolutionary within trade-expansion

indicators.note: within puts the radical word inside the word for a business upturn

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid growth in trade
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Economic growth is so dull it feels like a political uprising inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' places RED inside BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the tired, listless state of having nothing interesting to do.

clue.text: Fortunate, even without so much in retirement

indicators.note: in places the smaller amount inside the place of rest

parts.note: going to bed is retiring for the night, so bed stands for retirement
having less is going without so much

explanation.surface: Someone counts their luck while living on less after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but here it is retiring to BED; 'in' puts LESS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blessed is to be lucky or favoured, enjoying good fortune.

clue.text: Sheets of paper lying about before noon

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday

explanation.surface: Pages left scattered about on a desk in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' only joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a stationery quantity of five hundred sheets.

clue.text: Boring thing to train recruits?

parts.note: sounds like a tedious parade-ground routine for new soldiers, but describes a device that bores holes

explanation.walkthrough: To drill recruits is to train them; 'boring' means making holes, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilling machine is a powered tool for boring holes in metal, wood or rock.

clue.text: Get wind of mistrial after I leave

indicators.note: leave says the named letter departs from the legal word

explanation.surface: Someone hears rumours of a botched court case once they have quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get wind of' reads as one phrase, but 'wind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Science of simple fractions, perhaps?

parts.note: simple is read as unmixed or abstract, and fractions as a sample topic of the theoretical number discipline

explanation.definitionFit: Pure mathematics is the study of number and form for its own sake, without practical application.

clue.text: Organ left in Essex, for example

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A church organ installed somewhere in the county of Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is not the county here but the title: the Earl of Essex, such as Elizabeth I's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the noble titles of a British peer of that rank.

clue.text: No work in Derbyshire town? That's the finish!

indicators.note: No tells us to drop the work from the town name

parts.note: Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, northern England
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A town in Derbyshire with no jobs is all over.
explanation.walkthrough: GLOSSOP is a town in Derbyshire, an English county; 'No' removes OP from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloss is a shiny surface coating, the final finish of paint or varnish.

clue.text: A disgrace to speak indistinctly

definitions.meaning: an insult or stain on someone's reputation
to run words together when talking

explanation.surface: A drunk's mumbling brings shame on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an aspersion cast on someone, and to mumble words so they run into one another.

clue.text: Way to tear such a piece off?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for Street, a way
to rip is to tear

explanation.surface: A method for ripping a section off something.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a long narrow piece, the kind torn off a sheet.

clue.text: Ploughman's course?

parts.note: suggests the track a farmer follows across a field, but means the meal named after him in pubs

explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is the one where a ploughman's of bread and cheese is served.

clue.text: One who flies a way rise

parts.note: via is Latin for way or road
a tor is a rocky hill or rise

explanation.surface: A traveller takes to the air by a route that climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who operates an aircraft.

clue.text: Daily run laid out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of run laid are disordered

explanation.surface: An everyday jog has been mapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means happening every day, or active during daytime.

clue.text: Tip given to hatter

parts.note: reads as a gratuity handed to a milliner, but splits as the head measurement a hat maker needs

explanation.walkthrough: Split as CAP SIZE it is what a hatter is told; as one word it means to tip over.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to overturn, as a boat tips over in the water.

clue.text: E.g.Derby form with initial signs of improved competence

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: initial signs of tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A school form shows the first signs of getting better at a horse-racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English flat horse race at Epsom, one of the five races called the Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the British Classics, the five major races for three-year-old horses.

clue.text: Ability to understand others and pay them properly

indicators.note: properly suggests sorting the letters of pay them into the right order

explanation.surface: Fellow feeling, and paying people fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the capacity to share and feel another person's emotions.

clue.text: This point could be claimed

indicators.note: could be hints the word claimed may become something else once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain argument might be asserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point separates whole numbers from fractions in a written number.

clue.text: Despair in Slough?

definitions.meaning: the bog in Pilgrim's Progress, a swamp of hopelessness

explanation.surface: Gloom in a dreary English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town; it is the Slough of Despond, the bog of despair in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for hopelessness, and Bunyan named his swamp of despair after it.

clue.text: Throat-medicine for cheerleader in fresh insult

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the rearranged word
fresh means insult is made anew with its letters rearranged

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of cheer is C

explanation.surface: A cough remedy is offered to a cheerleader amid a new taunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes LINTUS from INSULT, and 'in' puts C (the first letter of cheer) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a thick syrupy cough mixture to soothe a sore throat.

clue.text: Greedy for a tanner?

parts.note: a tanner was old British slang for a sixpence, written VI d in Roman numerals plus d for pence

explanation.surface: Eager to get hold of a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was a sixpenny coin in pre-1971 British money; six pence is VI D.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, hungry to have something.

clue.text: A ship-wreck affected

indicators.note: wreck signals that the letters of a ship are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A vessel's ruin moved someone deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' suggests emotionally moved, but here means imitative, like a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish behaviour copies others foolishly, so it is mannered and put on.

clue.text: Part of relic on a religious symbol

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fragment of a holy relic serves as an emblem of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred image of Christ or a saint, venerated in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: River a number of sailors love

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is a body of sailors
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A river that a crew of seamen adore.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arno is the river through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is a river of Tuscany flowing through Florence to the sea.

clue.text: Taking exercise in outskirts of Southend, bowled along

indicators.note: in places the gym-class letters inside the outer pair
outskirts of means only the outer letters of the town name are used

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone working out on the edge of an Essex resort drove fast along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives S and D, the first and last letters of Southend.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl along is to travel quickly and smoothly, which is what speeding means.

clue.text: Limit of endurance out in rain, at spot that is stormy

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters are tossed about as in a tempest

explanation.surface: Caught in a downpour at a weather-beaten place, someone reaches the end of their tether.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturation point is the stage beyond which nothing more can be absorbed or tolerated.

clue.text: Brief nursery-rhyme?

definitions.meaning: a word that rhymes with nursery

explanation.surface: A short children's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery-rhyme' looks like a children's song but means a word rhyming with nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursory means hasty and superficial, and the word chimes with nursery.

clue.text: Variety of odd jewels to make a fair attraction

indicators.note: variety of suggests an assortment, so the letters of odd are mixed

parts.note: gems are jewels

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of strange jewellery becomes a sideshow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgems are bumper cars, a ride at funfairs.
